newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Pool starts C$6 mln capital upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Sask Pool starts C$6 mln capital upgrade.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handling firm on Thursday said started a C$6 million upgrade to its elevator in this southeast Saskatchewan town.

"This project underscores the depth of our commitment to producers in the Weyburn area and the entire southeast part of the province," Saskatchewan Wheat Pool chief executive Don Loewen said in a company statement.

The capital upgrade began immediately with construction and the addition of a 50-tonne an hour grain dryer. The first phase was scheduled to end in August, 1998. A second phase requiring another C$2.4 million was scheduled to end in 2000.

Phase two involve speeding up the facility's receiving capabilities and further expanding storage to address anticipated rail line abandonments and changing grain patterns within the industry, the SWP statement said.
Phase one will increase the elevator's car spot to 112 hopper cars from the current 39. Export-standard cleaning capacity will be 120 tonnes per hour.
A full-time mobile elevator will be stationed at the facility.
Hours of operation will be 16 hours a day, six days a week with 24 hour service available in peak periods.
